newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CBA sees good home lending returns.
newsitem.headline: CBA sees good home lending returns.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) said on Tuesday that it was achieving more sustainable returns from home lending with good volumes, improving market share and slower turnover of its loan portfolio.

CBA Managing Director David Murray told the bank's annual meeting the bank had planned to derive more sustainable returns from home lending when the government sold its remaining 50.4 percent stake in the bank earlier this year.
"At this early stage this looks attainable with good business volumes improving market share and slower turnover of the loan portfolio," Murray said in a speech to the meeting.
Murray said the bank's second objective had been to improve returns from other classes of business subsidised from home lending, notably retail transaction accounts.
"Although recent developments are encouraging, we still cannot rule out government intervention in the pricing of these accounts," he said.
"Further, since May, the gap between the wholesale cost of funds and the government deeming rate has narrowed, further accentuating the problem," he said.
Murray repeated comments by CBA chairman Tim Besley that the profit outlook remained flat and that 1996/97 would be every bid as challenging as previously expected.

Besley told the meeting the three main issues confronting the bank in 1996/97 were the home loan market, the role of technology in blurring the boundaries between financial service providers and the Wallis inquiry into the financial system.
"The home loan market remains intensely competitive," Besley said, adding that the bank had made clear during 1995/96 its intention to remain a leading provider of home loans.
